alert: Postgres connection pool exhausted; payment requests timing out
logs:
2026-07-21T01:18:03Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-c7mnr ERROR db.pool - timeout acquiring connection after 30000ms
2026-07-21T01:18:10Z pgbouncer-7f6c89c6d8-q4vmt LOG pool=payments cl_active=197 cl_waiting=96 sv_active=64
2026-07-21T01:18:17Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-c7mnr ERROR sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit reached
2026-07-21T01:18:25Z checkout-service-5b77d8c4f9-m8qkt ERROR pq: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
2026-07-21T01:18:41Z payments-api-6c8d7f5b9-c7mnr WARN POST /v1/payments status=503 reason=database_connection_timeout
root_cause: The nightly batch consumed the available pgbouncer server connections and left insufficient database capacity for interactive payment traffic.

actions.step: Scale the payments-api deployment to add more serving pods.
Increase PostgreSQL max_connections while the batch remains active.
Pause the nightly batch and restart pgbouncer to recover the connection pool.

postmortem: The overnight batch consumed the shared database pool and caused payment requests to wait beyond their connection timeout. Application scaling did not remove the database bottleneck, while pausing the batch and restarting pgbouncer restored capacity.

root_cause: An abandoned PostgreSQL replication slot retained excessive WAL and consumed nearly all free storage.

actions.step: Delete archived PostgreSQL and application logs to free disk space.
Drop the abandoned replication slot after confirming it was obsolete.
Expand the PostgreSQL PVC to provide additional storage capacity.

postmortem: An unused replication slot retained a large WAL backlog and filled the database filesystem. Removing the slot released the retained WAL, and PVC expansion restored additional storage headroom.

root_cause: PayFlow response latency exceeded the configured application deadline and caused payment requests to time out.

actions.step: Increase the PayFlow client timeout from five seconds to fifteen seconds.
Enable exponential backoff retries together with the PayFlow circuit breaker.
Fail over payment traffic to the secondary gateway.

postmortem: Elevated PayFlow latency caused payment requests to exceed their client deadlines. Raising the timeout did not stabilize the dependency, while protected retries and secondary-gateway failover restored successful payment processing.

root_cause: A scheduled processing workload exhausted the shared pgbouncer server pool and prevented interactive services from acquiring PostgreSQL connections.
